findings.finding: The single-analyst bar of $1.21 adjusted EPS implies -23.4% y/y against Q4 FY25's $1.58, while nine-month FY26 adjusted EPS was $2.65 against roughly $2.69 a year earlier (-1.5%), Q3 adjusted EPS fell only 2% with gross margin +250bp (35.5% vs 33.0%) and Apollo savings ahead of plan, and the share count is down (18.68M now vs ~19.4M a year ago after $74M of buybacks in FY26); the same analyst bar was $1.19 for Q4 FY25 (actual $1.58) and ~$1.70 for Q3 FY26 (actual $1.96), so an EPS beat is the likely print, which the market partly expects.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats are not reliably bought: Q4 FY25 beat $1.58 vs $1.19 closed +1.13%; Q2 FY26 adj EPS +14% y/y closed -7.01%; Q3 FY26 beat by ~15% closed +7.66%.
findings.why_not_priced: Only one estimate exists and it has lowballed the last two quarters; if the market priced a ~$1.40 print, previews would cite a higher bar than $1.21 and Earnings Whispers would not describe sentiment as bearish. Partly priced: the stock ran +14.6% in the month to 2026-11-04 and P/E is 34.5x, which is consistent with buyers already expecting another beat.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (consensus -23.4% y/y, 'the Street's caution sits below the gross profit line'): https://finviz.com/news/420699/jj-snack-foods-must-show-apollo-savings-can-outrun-freight-as-fy27-growth-pledge-nears; Q4 FY25 release for the $1.58 base and the $1.19 beat: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/785956/000143774925035287/ex_889324.htm

findings.finding: Theater attendance in JJSF's Q4 window (July-September 2026) was sharply up: Cinemark domestic attendance +12.7% to 37.4M with domestic concession per patron +5.6%, and AMC U.S. attendance +23.3% to 52.1M; a year earlier the same quarter's Frozen Beverages segment fell 8.3% to $99.6M with beverage sales -12.9% 'mainly from lower theater volumes' on box office down ~11%, and in Q3 FY26 beverage sales were already +$4.2M while machine (-$7.3M) and service (-$3.4M) sales drove the segment decline.
findings.link: Theaters are ICEE's frozen-beverage customers; Frozen Beverages was 23.2% of FY25 sales and its Q4 FY25 decline was attributed by the company to theater volumes. Theater share of beverage sales not found. Net of the rest: machine and service sales fell $10.7M in Q3 and management only expected to begin closing that gap in Q4, and convenience-store ICEE volume is soft (separate finding).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 frozen beverages -8.3% alongside a revenue miss closed +1.13%; segment-level reactions not isolable.
findings.source_date: on or before 2026-11-09 (Cinemark 8-K for quarter ended 2026-09-30; reported by https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/09/why-cinemark-stock-is-up-today/)
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue $400.5M (-2.4% y/y) leaves room for Frozen Beverages to swing several million; no preview found that quantifies the theater lap against the Q4 FY25 beverage -12.9%. If priced, previews would call out an easy frozen-beverage comp and the revenue bar would sit above prior-year Food Service drag math.
findings.independence: AMC Q3 2026: U.S. attendance +23.3%, F&B per patron $7.87 vs $7.74 (https://247wallst.com/cards/amc-entertainment-q3-2026-earnings-amc-01m6m76a69trkpjs9sq35vcjj5, snippet_only); management on 2026-08-05 said it was 'extremely encouraged by the movie lineup for the fourth quarter' (call, via search snippet of https://statementdog.com/analysis/JJSF/earnings_calls/317730).

findings.finding: Diesel averaged $6.291/gal in September 2026, a record monthly average and ~68% above September 2025, and reefer contract rates were $3.58/mile, +$0.82 y/y (reefer spot $3.62, +$1.18 y/y); on 2026-08-05 management reported +$4.7M of net freight/fuel cost in Q3, said pressure would persist into Q4 but that diesel had 'moderated from earlier summer highs', so the Q4 and early-FY27 freight hit is likely larger than management described.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 print with a $3.5M second-half fuel warning closed -7.01% despite adj EPS +14% y/y.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the consensus -23% EPS decline is explained by the preview as freight caution below gross profit. What is not priced is the size after the call: management's 'moderated' description was overtaken by a September record; if priced, the stock would not have run +14.6% in the month to 2026-11-04.
findings.independence: Magnus September 2026 diesel index, $6.29, +68% y/y (https://www.ajot.com/news/magnus-technologies-releases-september-2026-diesel-fuel-index-revealing-a-widening-fuel-surcharge-gap-as-diesel-nears-this-years-high, snippet_only); company's own freight statement in the Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000785956/000143774926025782/ex_998849.htm). Proxy: transmission to JJSF's own cost line is not confirmed for Q4.

findings.finding: Convenience-store traffic is cited as soft because of high fuel prices, and frozen-beverage sales in convenience stores were flagged as a soft area into Q4; c-stores are ICEE's other main channel beside theaters.
findings.why_not_priced: Named in previews, so largely priced; filed small because no channel number exists to size it and it offsets part of the theater tailwind.
findings.independence: Simply Wall St/Webull note naming 'softer convenience store traffic linked to higher oil prices' (https://www.webull.com/news/15870231967407104, 2026-11-05). Shares a theme with the diesel finding but a different line (sales vs cost).

findings.finding: The stock ran +14.6% in the month to a $91.01 close on 2026-11-04 (+4.6% that day, no identified news) and +9.7% since the August print against an S&P 500 down ~3%, to a P/E of 34.5x against 18.1x for US Food; it has since eased to $88.70 (5-day -0.81%), so the market's real bar sits above the $1.21 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into Q3 FY26 the stock had also drifted up and still rose +7.66% on the beat; into Q1 FY26 it fell -15.44% on a sales decline.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself; it says the beat is expected. It is a finding about the reaction: a beat on the $1.21 bar alone may not lift a name that rerated 15% in a month without news.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers: +10.7% since the last report vs S&P -3%, post-earnings drift +9.7% (https://finviz.com/news/420699/jj-snack-foods-must-show-apollo-savings-can-outrun-freight-as-fy27-growth-pledge-nears; https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/JJSF); baseline run_up_20d_pct +8.41.

findings.finding: Sysco, a broadline distributor through which foodservice snack makers sell, reported U.S. Foodservice case volume +2.6% and local +2.7% for the 13 weeks ended 2026-09-26 (the same weeks as JJSF's Q4), above its own guide, though restaurant traffic was weak and August softened.
findings.link: Distribution channel: JJSF's Food Service segment (63.3% of FY25 sales) sells soft pretzels, churros and handhelds to restaurants, schools, stadiums and other foodservice outlets, partly through broadline distributors; JJSF's share of Sysco volume not found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Food Service drove the Q1-Q3 FY26 sales declines (bakery exit); reaction history for this line is the -15.44%/-7.01% on sales declines.
findings.why_not_priced: A broad channel series that JJSF previews do not cite; small because JJSF's Food Service decline is mostly its own planned bakery exit (~$16M in Q3), not channel volume.
findings.independence: Peer foodservice read in the next finding points the other way; none in the same direction.

findings.finding: Marzetti (formerly Lancaster Colony) reported foodservice revenue -7% to $229M and foodservice volume -7.6% for the quarter ended 2026-09-30, of which about 4.3 points was the end of a temporary Winland supply agreement, leaving an underlying decline near -3%.
findings.link: Same channel (U.S. restaurant foodservice, packaged food supplier), different products (dressings, sauces, bread); no shared customer figure found.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer print after JJSF last spoke, not cited in JJSF previews; aggregator source, not verified against the 8-K, so filed small.
findings.independence: Sysco finding points the other way on channel volume; Sysco also noted weak restaurant traffic (https://finviz.com/news/414229/sysco-reports-first-quarter-2027-results-reiterates-fy27-adjusted-eps-and-local-volume-guidance).

findings.finding: Management has stated the FY27 top-line growth claim each quarter and on 2026-08-05 said bakery headwinds would diminish in Q4 (preview: drag from ~3.5% to ~2.5% of sales), no further SKU rationalization is planned, and no capacity investment is needed for the growth; with the theater tailwind landing, a qualitative reaffirmation (not a numeric guide, which the company has never given) is the likely next-guide outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 FY26 release that first framed 'return to top-line growth in fiscal 2027' closed +7.66% on a revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The growth claim is public and partly priced in the run-up; what is not knowable is whether record diesel makes management hedge FY27 margin commentary. Range is wide on purpose: the guide is where the reaction is decided.
findings.independence: Company release quote 'a return to top-line growth in fiscal 2027' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000785956/000143774926025782/ex_998849.htm) is the same statement in a second document; EW preview on drag easing (https://finviz.com/news/420699/jj-snack-foods-must-show-apollo-savings-can-outrun-freight-as-fy27-growth-pledge-nears).

findings.finding: On 2026-06-04/05 JJSF amended its revolver: maturity extended to 2031-06-05, maximum net leverage raised from 3.00x to 3.50x (to 4.00x for four quarters after an acquisition over $50M, usable twice), accordion up to the greater of $200M or consolidated EBITDA; the company ended FY25 with $106M cash and no debt, so this is acquisition capacity, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2022 Dippin' Dots acquisition ($222M) was announced outside a print; no print-day M&A precedent found.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for five months; it only matters if a deal is announced with the print, and nothing found says one is. What the money buys: unanswered (no deal found), so sized 0. The same 8-K reports the General Counsel's resignation effective 2026-06-30.

findings.why_not_priced: Five days to cover on a ~$17M/day name is a modest squeeze mechanism; not crowded, and already shrinking, so small.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew; the evidence on the quarter (bar likely beaten, theater tailwind) leans positive while the +8.4% 20-day / +14.6% one-month run-up and the record freight cut against it, so the net is close to zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): EPS-beat finding shrunk +1.5 -> +1.0 because this name's beats have closed +1.1% and -7.0% as well as +7.7%; the separate reaction-history finding (-0.3) was merged into it as a duplicate so the lesson is applied once; p_up 54 -> 53.
Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): freight finding shrunk -1.5 -> -1.0 because management had already said freight pressure would persist into Q4 and the -23% consensus embeds it.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): theater finding shrunk +1.0 -> +0.8 for falling machine/service sales and soft c-store volume in the same segment.

Rule 6 bar check left standing: revenue bar agrees across three sources and EPS across two ($1.21/$1.22) with one $1.31 outlier, so sizes were not capped; Rule 7 checked: short interest 5.2% and falling, no crowded-short shrink needed; Rule 4: revolver amendment signed 0 after asking what it buys (no deal found).
